connections.why: Existing products are analysed to understand and refine design requirements
Clear requirements direct how ideas are generated and communicated
Analysing products exposes their social, ethical and environmental impact
Material properties determine which manufacturing processes can be used
Technical understanding of forces depends on knowing material properties
Knowledge of structures and scales of production shapes how things are made
Sustainability and social factors are part of judging a solution's viability
Ideas are evaluated against viability to decide which to take forward
Core design-thinking skills are applied directly to set problems
Material knowledge is the basis for selecting materials in a problem context
Viability principles are reapplied when evaluating problem-solving solutions
Applied design thinking begins with exploring and framing the NEA context
Selecting materials and processes underpins the make phase of the NEA
Evaluation skills are central to the iterative testing of the NEA
Exploration of the context leads into designing and making
Each prototype is tested and refined in the iterative cycle
